title: 2-Year Floating Rate Note auction (reopening of the July new issue, series BF-2028)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF, text layer decompressed and rebuilt from per-glyph Td/Tm coordinates direct 2026-09-05 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) — row reads `2-Year FRN R / Announcement Thursday, September 17, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, September 23, 2026 / Settlement Friday, September 25, 2026`, the `R` marker identifying it as a reopening (the 2026-10-28 and 2027-01-27 rows in the same PDF drop it). Size corroborated in advance by press release sb0590 (2026-08-05), re-read as text direct 2026-09-05, whose Sep-26 anticipated-size row reads 28 in the FRN column (header `2-Year 3-Year 5-Year 7-Year 10-Year 20-Year 30-Year FRN`, row `69 58 70 44 39 13 22 28`), introduced verbatim as `the anticipated auction sizes for the August to October 2026 quarter`; the auction record agrees independently, with 20 consecutive reopenings at $28B since 2024-05-29 (fiscaldata auctions_query, floating_rate:Yes, 154 rows, pulled 2026-09-05). Stays estimate on two counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-09-17 announcement itself. The 11:30 ET auction slot IS sourced, unusually for this calendar: fiscaldata publishes `closing_time_comp`, which reads `11:30 AM` on 137 of the 154 FRN auctions since 2014, every exception being a holiday or short week
notes: The only 2-Year FRN auction between 2026-09-05 and the treasury-2y-frn-2026-10-28 quarterly new issue, and therefore the single free read on whether that event's premise survives: the FRN discount margin is at a four-year low (5.0bp on 2026-07-29, 5.5bp on 2026-08-26; last sub-5.0bp print 2022-07-27) and the 10-28 ledger's inherited kill switch is this auction printing a high discount margin above 10.0bp. Read it for the margin and nothing else. A reopening is categorically the LESSER of the two events and is filed at `low` impact for that reason: measured across the complete 154-auction series, a new issue's high discount margin BECOMES the note's coupon spread (51/51, no exception since 2014) and every reopening of that CUSIP inherits it (103/103) — so this auction's own margin is a market mark that changes nothing, while 10-28 stamps a two-year contract on roughly $86B. This one reopens series BF-2028, whose spread was fixed at 0.0500 on 2026-07-29; expect `spread` to print 0.0500 again regardless of where the margin lands. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. Discovered during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-22 initial research (2026-09-05), which named it and deliberately left it unfiled as outside its own corridor; filed by the treasury-2y-frn-2026-10-28 initial research the same day, for which it is the one dated intermediate check.
